## InfoTB 0.2.0 alpha

### iPhone: a completely new, native app

The iOS interface has been rewritten from scratch in **SwiftUI**, so InfoTB now looks and feels like a premium iPhone app rather than a port.

- **Liquid Glass on iOS 26+**: the tab bar, toolbars, sheets, menus, map controls and search all use the new system material (with a frosted fallback on iOS 17–18).
- **Apple Maps**: line routes and stops are drawn natively with MapKit, with smooth pinch and zoom, dark mode, and direction arrows along the route.
  - Tap a stop on the map to see when this line arrives there next, then jump to the stop page. Going back returns you to the map where you left it.
  - The header shows the line and where it's heading.
- **Dashboard**: live countdowns, notices on the cards they affect, and a native edit mode where you drag to reorder, swipe to delete and hide cards or whole groups. Card options and groups (including active hours) open in sheets.
- **Lines**: transport-type and night filter chips plus a search field at the bottom, within thumb reach. Swipe a line to favourite it.
- **Line page**: Tour/Retour picker, a live "N vehicles live" indicator, and the stop timeline showing approaching vehicles.
- **Settings**: a native settings form with backup and restore through the Files app.
- **Dynamic Island & Live Activities** keep working as before, now started from the native bell buttons.
- Requires **iOS 17** or later.

### Both platforms

- **Metro lines in their real colours**: M1 yellow, M2 blue, M3 red, M4 green and both M5 branches orange (the API sends the same dark grey for all of them). Badge text switches to black on yellow so it stays readable.
- Shared logic (view models, arrival tracking) now lives in one Kotlin module used by both apps.

### Notes

- **Android** keeps its Compose interface and Leaflet/OpenStreetMap maps in this release.
- The **IPA is unsigned**; install it with [iLoader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader) or Sideloadly. See [Building & releasing](https://github.com/dev-andrei-v/infotb-modern-client/blob/v0.2.0-alpha/docs/building.md#ios-sideloading) for which tools support the Dynamic Island.
- Known: metro stations don't show arrivals on their stop page, and the small stop map may be missing while STB's coordinates endpoint returns errors.
